matthew.label: ~6 - 4 BCE
matthew.note: Blumell and Wayment place the birth before Herod died in spring 4 BC, probably no earlier than 6 BC. Matthew 2 ends after Herod's death. The Church table gives no year.

matthew.label: ~27 - 33 CE
matthew.note: Chadwick starts the ministry at Passover AD 28, after John began in late AD 27. Others date the crucifixion to AD 33. The range covers both views.

matthew.label: ~30 - 33 CE
matthew.note: Chadwick argues for April AD 30. He reports that others, such as Humphreys and Waddington, favor AD 33. The Church table leaves the Crucifixion year blank.

mark.label: ~27 - 33 CE
mark.note: Mark starts with John the Baptist. Ministry dates depend on an AD 30 or AD 33 crucifixion. Martin notes the synoptic Gospels imply a shorter ministry than John.

mark.label: ~30 - 33 CE
mark.note: The passion week. Chadwick argues for AD 30 and names AD 33 as the main other view. The Church table gives no year.

luke.label: ~7 BCE - 8 CE
luke.note: Luke 1 starts before John's birth; Luke 2 ends with Jesus at twelve. Blumell and Wayment place the birth about 6-4 BC. They find the AD 6 Quirinius census hard to fit.

luke.label: ~27 - 33 CE
luke.note: Luke 3:1 dates John to Tiberius's fifteenth year. Chadwick reckons it as autumn AD 27 to autumn AD 28. The label now matches Matthew and Mark.

luke.label: ~30 - 33 CE
luke.note: The passion and resurrection. Chadwick argues for AD 30 and reports AD 33 as the main other view.

john.label: ~27 - 33 CE
john.note: Martin notes John names three Passovers, so the ministry lasts over two years. Chadwick uses them for Passover AD 28 to AD 30. Others end it in AD 33.

john.label: ~30 - 33 CE
john.note: The last supper, death, and appearances. John puts the crucifixion the day before Passover. Chadwick dates it to April AD 30; others prefer AD 33.

acts.label: ~30 - 34 CE
acts.note: Starts after the crucifixion (AD 30 or 33). Frederick dates Paul's conversion about AD 34; the Church table says AD 35. Stephen dies before it.

acts.label: ~34 - 44 CE
acts.note: Paul's conversion is about AD 34-35. The Church table dates the deaths of James and Herod Agrippa I (Acts 12) to AD 44.

acts.label: ~45 - 49 CE
acts.note: The Church table dates the first missionary tour to AD 45. Frederick dates it about AD 48-49. The label covers both.

acts.label: ~49 - 50 CE
acts.note: The Church table and Frederick date the Jerusalem council to AD 49. The Bible Dictionary says about AD 50.

acts.label: ~49 - 53 CE
acts.note: Frederick dates the second mission about AD 50-52. He dates Gallio (Acts 18:12) to spring AD 51-52. Elledge places Paul's Corinth stay in AD 50-51.

acts.label: ~53 - 57 CE
acts.note: Frederick dates the third mission, with about three years in Ephesus, to AD 53-56. He places the return to Jerusalem about AD 57.

acts.label: ~57 - 60 CE
acts.note: Frederick dates the arrest about AD 57 and Caesarea about AD 58-60. The Church table has AD 57-58. Festus's start date differs by source.

acts.label: ~58 - 62 CE
acts.note: The Church table sends Paul to Rome in AD 58 and closes Acts in AD 61. Frederick dates the Roman imprisonment about AD 60-62.

romans.label: ~55 - 57 CE
romans.note: Written from Corinth before the trip to Jerusalem. The Bible Dictionary says AD 55-56; Judd says about AD 53-56. Frederick dates the arrest about AD 57.

1-corinthians.label: ~53 - 56 CE
1-corinthians.note: Written near the end of Paul's stay in Ephesus. Judd dates it about AD 52-56; the Bible Dictionary says AD 55-56.

2-corinthians.label: ~55 - 56 CE
2-corinthians.note: The Bible Dictionary places it in Macedonia, AD 55-56; Judd says about AD 53-56. Hodge reports that many scholars see two or more joined letters.

galatians.label: ~49 - 56 CE
galatians.note: Judd and Frederick date it about AD 49-50, soon after the council. The Bible Dictionary places it with Corinthians and Romans, AD 55-56. Frederick says the date is debated.

ephesians.label: ~60 CE or later (disputed)
ephesians.note: Traditional view: Paul wrote it in prison, about AD 58-62. Martin and Concannon report that many think a later disciple wrote it. These sources give no later year.

philippians.label: ~58 - 62 CE
philippians.note: Written in prison. Judd dates it about AD 58-62 and says most scholars place it in Rome. He notes another city is possible.

colossians.label: ~60 CE or later (disputed)
colossians.note: Traditional view: Paul wrote it in prison, about AD 58-62. Martin thinks a disciple of Paul wrote it later. These sources give no later year.

1-thessalonians.label: ~50 - 52 CE
1-thessalonians.note: Written from Corinth soon after Paul left Thessalonica. The Church table says AD 50; the Bible Dictionary says AD 50-51; Judd says about AD 50-52.

2-thessalonians.label: ~51 CE or later (disputed)
2-thessalonians.note: Traditional view: soon after 1 Thessalonians, about AD 50-52. Martin and Concannon report that many scholars think someone else wrote it. They give no year.

1-timothy.label: ~60s CE or 2nd century (disputed)
1-timothy.note: Traditional view: Paul, about AD 60-65. Martin says most scholars think another writer composed the Pastorals. He guesses the mid-second century.

2-timothy.label: ~60s CE or 2nd century (disputed)
2-timothy.note: Traditional view: Paul's last letter, from a second Roman imprisonment, about AD 64-65. Martin dates the Pastorals much later, probably the mid-second century.

titus.label: ~60s CE or 2nd century (disputed)
titus.note: Traditional view: Paul, about AD 60-65. Martin and Concannon report that most scholars think the Pastorals came from a later writer.

philemon.label: ~58 - 62 CE
philemon.note: Written in prison. Judd dates it about AD 58-62; the Bible Dictionary says AD 60-62 in Rome. Judd does not name the city.

hebrews.label: ~60 - 100 CE
hebrews.note: Blumell, Judd, and Pierce give AD 60-100, likely before AD 70. The Bible Dictionary groups it with AD 60-62. Martin says the author is unknown.

james.label: Date unknown (disputed)
james.note: The Bible Dictionary says the date is not known. The RSC chapter suggests the 40s AD. Stewart Lester lists James among letters scholars call pseudepigraphic.

1-peter.label: ~60 - 100 CE
1-peter.note: The Bible Dictionary dates it soon after AD 64. Green allows Peter in the early 60s or a later writer in the first century. Martin doubts Peter wrote it.

2-peter.label: ~60s CE or 2nd century (disputed)
2-peter.note: Traditional view: before Peter's death, about AD 64-68. Hultin suggests the late first or well into the second century. Martin says the second century.

1-john.label: ~70 - 100 CE
1-john.note: The RSC chapter gives about AD 70-100; it says most scholars favor the 90s. The Bible Dictionary and Martin both place it after the Gospel of John.

2-john.label: ~70 - 100 CE
2-john.note: The RSC chapter gives about AD 70-100 for all three letters. Martin places 2 and 3 John after 1 John.

3-john.label: ~70 - 100 CE
3-john.note: The RSC chapter gives about AD 70-100 for all three letters. Martin places 2 and 3 John after 1 John.

jude.label: Date unknown
jude.note: The Bible Dictionary gives no date. The RSC chapter places it before Jude's traditional death about AD 65. Hultin says 2 Peter borrows from Jude.

revelation.label: ~68 - 96 CE
revelation.note: Martin says some date it to Nero's time, but more place it late in the century. Kirby favors late Domitian (AD 81-96). The Bible Dictionary says the date is unknown.
